From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. 1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller draft and Disclosure Letter

**Threshold note:** The Seller's "[STANDARD]/FINAL" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" are the other side's advocacy, not an agreed position and not an instruction to this review. Nothing in the Buyer's record confirms principal-level sign-off on the limitation package. Every issue below is treated as open. The Disclosure Letter is actually helpful to us: paragraphs 2–6 confirm, in the Seller's own words, that key consents, the discharge, the Ironquay assignment and the bonus funding are all unresolved.

---

**SPA-N-001 – General liability cap (cl 12.1)**
- Seller: 20% of price (AUD 4.8m), applied across all claims.
- Buyer wants: General warranties capped at 100% of price (fallback 50%, with W&I pricing if available); cap does not apply to fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities or fraud.
- Recommend: Reject 20% as an across-the-board cap; counter at 100%, or accept a lower general cap only if fundamental/tax/indemnities are carved out at 100%+. Reason: known live exposures (Riverlark 3.2m, Bluefen 3.6m revenue at risk, bonuses, privacy) could alone exhaust 4.8m.

**SPA-N-002 – De minimis & basket (cl 12.2)**
- Seller: AUD 25k de minimis, AUD 250k basket, excess-only recovery.
- Buyer wants: De minimis ~AUD 10k; basket ~AUD 120–240k (0.5–1%) as a tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded); related claims aggregated; no thresholds for fundamental, tax, indemnity or fraud claims.
- Recommend: Counter at AUD 10k / AUD 240k tipping, with aggregation of same-cause claims. Reason: the Seller's structure wipes out AUD 250k of real loss and the 25k de minimis would exclude typical SaaS-level claims.

**SPA-N-003 – General claims time limit (cl 12.3/13)**
- Seller: 18 months, and all limitations apply to all claims unless expressly excluded.
- Buyer wants: 24 months for general warranties (covering two audit cycles); 7 years for tax and fundamental; indemnities tied to the underlying statutory limitation; notice period preserves the claim provided proceedings follow within 6–9 months.
- Recommend: Counter at 24 months general / 7 years tax and fundamental; delete the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" default and replace with the reverse presumption. Reason: 18 months expires before the second post-Completion audit and would catch tax reviews that typically surface later.

**SPA-N-004 – Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- Buyer wants: Title, capacity, authority and no-encumbrance warranties capped at 100% of price, 6–7 year limitation, no de minimis/basket, not subject to disclosure or knowledge qualifiers.
- Recommend: Reject outright. Reason: a 20% cap on title means the Buyer pays AUD 24m for shares it might not own and recovers at most 4.8m.

**SPA-N-005 – Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: None. Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature".
- Buyer wants: Express carve-out from every cap, threshold, time limit, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clause for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and wilful default by the Seller or its officers/advisers.
- Recommend: Insist as non-negotiable. Reason: a clause purporting to limit liability for fraud is unenforceable in any event, but its absence invites argument and signals the Seller is drafting to the edge.

**SPA-N-006 – Disclosure scope (Sch 7, DL [1.1]–[1.2])**
- Seller: General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and all public records; para [1.4] denies any admission.
- Buyer wants: Disclosure effective only if "fair, specific and with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter"; data room disclosed only as a fixed, indexed USB/schedule; public-register disclosure limited to named ASIC/PPSR/IP Australia searches on a stated date; no disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax warranties or indemnities.
- Recommend: Reject general data-room and open-ended public-record disclosure; counter with a fair-disclosure standard and a closed index. Reason: as drafted the Seller can defeat almost any claim by pointing to a document buried in the room.

**SPA-N-007 – Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)**
- Seller: No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or could have discovered from the data room or public records.
- Buyer wants: Delete. At most, limited to actual knowledge of 3–4 named deal-team individuals, excluding advisers and constructive/imputed knowledge, and not applying to specific indemnities, fundamental or tax warranties.
- Recommend: Delete; fallback is named-individual actual knowledge only. Reason: "discoverable" plus advisers' knowledge turns the warranty package into a near-nullity and penalises the Buyer for doing diligence.

**SPA-N-008 – Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3; DL para 2)**
- Seller: Reasonable endeavours; condition deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent. DL confirms no consent and no evidence cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- Buyer wants: Unconditional written consent from Bluefen (including satisfaction or waiver of cl 11.3 conditions) in form approved by the Buyer as a true condition precedent, with Seller on best/all reasonable endeavours, Buyer approval of any concessions, and long-stop protection; absent consent, price adjustment/escrow or right to walk.
- Recommend: Elevate to a CP in agreed form; do not accept a bare "written consent" trigger. Reason: ~30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6m) is tied to a contract that can be terminated on change of control.

**SPA-N-009 – Riverlark facility (cl 2/7; DL para 3)**
- Seller: AUD ~3.2m facility to be released "following Completion". DL confirms not repaid and no discharge.
- Buyer wants: Repayment at Completion out of the purchase price via funds flow, with executed deed of release/discharge and PPSR release delivered as Completion deliverables; price adjusted debt-free/cash-free accordingly; consent of Riverlark under cl 8.1 to the change of control obtained before Completion.
- Recommend: Reject post-Completion release; require payout letter, release and PPSR discharge at Completion. Reason: on a debt-free basis the Buyer would otherwise fund a company carrying 3.2m of secured debt and an unconsented change of control default.

**SPA-N-010 – Employee bonuses (DL para 5; funds flow)**
- Seller: AUD 420k Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow; silent on on-costs.
- Buyer wants: Bonuses plus superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs (estimate ~AUD 500k gross) treated as Seller transaction costs: either paid by the Seller before Completion or deducted from the price in the funds flow; specific indemnity for any shortfall or unfunded on-cost.
- Recommend: Insert as a price deduction in the funds flow, grossed up for on-costs, plus indemnity. Reason: the obligor is the target company, so absent adjustment the Buyer pays the Seller's bonuses twice (in price and in cash out of the company).

**SPA-N-011 – Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1; DL para 4)**
- Seller: Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; considered adequate. DL confirms AUD 180k open, no receipt, no confirmatory assignment.
- Buyer wants: Pre-Completion payment of the AUD 180k and delivery of a signed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable; indemnity covering loss of or defect in title to all SOW3 Project Materials and any third-party claims, outside cap/basket/time limits; fundamental-style IP ownership warranty uncapped by disclosure.
- Recommend: Require payment plus assignment at Completion; broaden indemnity and carve it out of limitations. Reason: under cl 7.3 the company does not own the SOW3 deliverables until paid, so a "payment-only" indemnity does not cover the real risk, which is loss of core IP.

**SPA-N-012 – Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL para 6)**
- Seller: "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. DL confirms ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification status unknown.
- Buyer wants: Completed investigation and written outcome before Completion (including OAIC/NDB assessment and, if required, notification); specific indemnity for all costs, regulatory penalties, customer claims and remediation, outside cap/basket/time limits and not subject to disclosure; warranty that no other incidents exist; covenant to conduct the investigation to Buyer's satisfaction.
- Recommend: Specific indemnity plus pre-Completion investigation closure. Reason: the disclosure is drafted to disclose the incident against the warranties while giving the Buyer nothing in return — classic disclosed-risk gap.

**SPA-N-013 – Sandbar renewals (DL para 8)**
- Seller: Three AUD 110k renewals (330k) are "ordinary-course operating costs"; disclosure declines to say whether they are avoidable or accrued.
- Buyer wants: Confirmation of renewal dates, termination rights and whether amounts are budgeted in the locked-box/working-capital reference; treat any renewal committed pre-Completion but benefiting post-Completion as a working-capital/debt-like item; warranty that no other related renewals exist.
- Recommend: Seek specific disclosure of terms; adjust working capital if the spend is accelerated or prepaid. Reason: three identical renewals split across two DD files looks like contract-splitting below a disclosure threshold and could be AUD 330k of debt-like cost shifted to the Buyer.

**SPA-N-014 – Category separation**
- Seller: One regime for everything — cap, thresholds, time limits, disclosure and knowledge all apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- Buyer wants: Four distinct tiers: (1) general warranties – negotiated cap/basket/time; (2) fundamental and title – 100%, 7 years, no basket, no disclosure; (3) tax – 100%, 7 years, no basket; (4) specific indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Bluefen) – AUD-for-AUD, outside all limitations, not subject to disclosure or knowledge.
- Recommend: Restructure cl 12 around these tiers. Reason: "administrative simplicity" is a label for collapsing the Buyer's strongest protections into the weakest regime.

**SPA-N-015 – Title verification (DL para 10)**
- Seller: Title evidenced by the company share register at DD-012; DL acknowledges the Buyer has not independently verified.
- Buyer wants: Independent ASIC company extract and historical share-register search on signing and Completion; PPSR search for security over the shares (Riverlark likely holds a share mortgage or all-asset charge); review of constitution for pre-emptive rights; executed transfer, original share certificate and board resolution as Completion deliverables; uncapped title warranty.
- Recommend: Run ASIC/PPSR searches now and before Completion; do not rely on the Seller's own register. Reason: an internal register is the Seller's document, not evidence, and the Riverlark security may extend to the shares.

**SPA-N-016 – Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: "Settled under the general regime" — i.e. 20% cap, 18 months, general disclosure.
- Buyer wants: Full tax warranty suite plus a tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, AUD-for-AUD, 100% cap, 7 years, no basket, not disclosure-qualified); IP warranties covering ownership of all software and Project Materials, no infringement, open-source compliance, employee/contractor assignments, with Ironquay carved into a specific indemnity.
- Recommend: Treat as genuinely open; table a tax indemnity and separate IP warranty schedule. Reason: for a SaaS business, IP and tax are the asset and the hidden liability, respectively — neither belongs under an 18-month, 20% regime.

---

**Priority for the mark-up (in order):** Riverlark release at Completion (N-009), Bluefen CP in agreed form (N-008), category separation with fundamental/tax/indemnity carve-outs (N-004/N-014/N-005), delete cl 8.3 and general disclosure (N-006/N-007), then the headline numbers (N-001/N-002/N-003). The specific items (bonuses, Ironquay, privacy, Sandbar) should be resolved by funds-flow adjustments and specific indemnities rather than left to the warranty package.
